content:
In recent years, Macs have become increasingly affordable. With lower starting prices, more RAM and storage per dollar, and the launch of the MacBook Neo, Apple has for the first time become one of the most value-for-money options on the market.

Unfortunately, due to the ongoing memory shortage, Apple has hiked prices significantly. Macs aren't as attractive as they were a few weeks ago, but there are still some decent deals out there — if you need a new computer, I still believe that, given the current state of the entire computer market, today's Mac is a solid choice.

MacBook Air

Before the MacBook Neo launched, the MacBook Air was the entry-level option in Apple's laptop lineup. The arrival of the MacBook Neo makes the MacBook Air's value-for-money positioning a little awkward, but if you want a better user experience without needing top-tier specs, I'd still say the MacBook Air is a very impressive laptop.

MagSafe charging, a P3 wide-colour-gamut display, a Center Stage camera, and longer battery life are just some of its selling points. It also comes in a 15-inch version, whereas the MacBook Neo is only available in 13-inch.

Right now, discounts across the entire MacBook Air lineup are as follows:

MacBook Neo

This product needs little introduction — the MacBook Neo is Apple's first affordable MacBook, priced at just $699.

Compared to the MacBook Air above, there are indeed some trade-offs, but at this price point it's still tremendous value. Build quality, display clarity, and the macOS experience have essentially not been compromised. Of course, you have to accept the slower A18 Pro chip (though to be honest it's not bad), fewer ports, and only 8GB of RAM, but at this price point that's entirely reasonable. It also comes in vibrant colour options such as Citrus Yellow, Blush, and Indigo.

There are no notable retail discounts on the MacBook Neo right now, but Apple does sell refurbished units for $100 to $120 less than retail. Apple refurbished products come with a one-year warranty, the user experience is essentially identical to a new unit, every major component has been replaced, there are no scratches, and no battery degradation issues.

  • MacBook Neo: 256GB storage, 8GB RAM — $689 at Amazon ($10 off)
  • MacBook Neo: 512GB storage, 8GB RAM, Touch ID — $789 at Amazon ($10 off)
  • Refurbished MacBook Neo: 256GB storage, 8GB RAM — $599 at Apple Store
  • Refurbished MacBook Neo: 512GB storage, 8GB RAM, Touch ID — $679 at Apple Store

MacBook Pro

The MacBook Pro is the flagship model in the lineup. You can get top-tier specs, but there's one important consideration. Apple is reportedly set to redesign its high-end MacBook Pro later this year, with an OLED display, touchscreen, and a thinner chassis.

However, this redesign will debut only on models equipped with M5 Pro and M5 Max chips — so if you're looking at the base M5 model, there's absolutely no problem buying a brand-new MacBook Pro right now. Even if you don't care about the redesign at all, the M5 Pro and M5 Max are still outstanding new chips.
